next_item_hypothesis: The selected demonstrated failure is sparse/tail next-item transitions: 339519 train transitions are distributed over 323633 directed pairs, and 314605 pairs (0.9266197178950221) have no observed reverse event. This motivates testing whether a negatively curved metric represents uneven, branching transition neighborhoods; it does not establish hierarchy, negative curvature, or causal improvement. The verified literature supports sequential next-item recommendation with generative semantic IDs only, not hyperbolic geometry.

math_definition.geometry_constants: Freeze curved c=1, flat c=0, delta=0.0, shared projection radius R=0.9, epsilon=1e-6, tau_assign=0.05, and 100 Sinkhorn iterations. No sweep. For c>0 define u=1+2c||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)); clamp u from below to 1.0 only, then arcosh(u)=log1p((u-1)+sqrt((u-1)(u+1))). The scored quantity is squared distance D_c^2=(1/c)*arcosh(u)^2. Both arms project to the same fixed ball before scoring; for c=1 this lies strictly inside the Poincare domain. At c=0 use the exact limit D_0^2=4||x-y||^2; unsquared distance tends to 2||x-y||. The exponential map's c-to-zero limit is identity but it is not used. The curvature-dependent radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at c=0; use the same fixed-radius projection in both arms instead.

c_dependent_rules_flat_limits.curvature_dependent_projection_radius_(1: undefined at c=0; both arms instead use the same fixed-radius projection norm<=0.9

operator.scoring: Use D_c^2, not unsquared distance. Score projected latent and projected code vectors directly; no exponential map. Curvature is the only arm switch in the scoring metric.

assignment_algorithm.population: All and only frozen training-split items in ascending immutable item-ID order; no minibatch, validation or test items.
assignment_algorithm.conditioning: At level l, independently within each nonempty group defined by exactly the already frozen labels (k1,...,k(l-1)); level 1 has no conditioning labels.
assignment_algorithm.cost_and_transport: In each group compute C[i,k]=D_c^2(P(z_i),P(e[l,k])) using that arm's metric on identically projected coordinates. Set logK[i,k]=-C[i,k]/0.05, row marginal a_i=1/n_group, column marginal b_k=1/256. In ascending item-ID/code-ID order initialize logv[k]=0 and perform exactly 100 log-domain iterations logu[i]=log(a_i)-LSE_k(logK[i,k]+logv[k]), then logv[k]=log(b_k)-LSE_i(logK[i,k]+logu[i]). Q[i,k]=exp(logK[i,k]+logu[i]+logv[k]) is the resulting deterministic soft transport target.
assignment_algorithm.discrete_label_extraction: Convert Q to a hard feasible assignment minimizing sum_i -log(Q[i,k_i]) subject to each code count being floor(n_group/256) or ceil(n_group/256); assign the remainder to lower code IDs. Solve the finite transportation problem exactly; among equal-cost optima choose the lexicographically smallest label vector in ascending item-ID order, with code-ID ascending as the final tie-break. This fixes every label deterministically. Empty parent groups are skipped; groups smaller than 256 still assign every item. Within each occupied parent group this maintains balanced child-code use, while global full-population soft-assignment entropy regularization prevents collapse of the level-one and level-two populations and directly preserves level-two prefix diversity.
assignment_algorithm.arm_and_refresh: Both arms use exactly this procedure, with only D_c^2 replaced by its c-to-zero limit in the flat arm; no shared curved labels. Use the frozen KMeans codebook initialization unchanged. At epoch zero calculate labels and Q from initialized parameters. At each subsequent epoch boundary calculate labels and Q from the current detached snapshot over the entire training item population; freeze q, Q for that whole epoch. No batch-dependent normalization.
assignment_algorithm.gradient_rule: Hard labels q and transport targets Q are stop-gradient. Differentiable logits and soft assignments s are recomputed from current parameters in the losses below; no loss relies on gradients through the frozen assignment.

objective.anti_collapse: L_bal is the full-training-population marginal KL-to-uniform of differentiable soft assignments, evaluated once per epoch and included in L_total with coefficient 1.0. It has gradients through s and penalizes unused codes, so assigning every item to one code cannot lower the objective; it supports global level-two prefix diversity rather than acting on frozen one-hot labels.

loss_equations.name: reconstruction
loss_equations.equation: L_rec=(1/(3*N)) sum_{i in I_train} sum_{l=1}^3 D_c^2(P(z_i),P(e[l,q[i,l]]))
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: z[N,32], e[3,256,32], q[N,3] frozen discrete labels; P is the shared fixed-radius projection.
loss_equations.index_normalization_reduction: Mean over training items and three levels; summed squared distances.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: Absent items contribute nothing; N=0 makes the objective invalid and NULL.
loss_equations.gradient_and_circularity: Gradient flows through projected z and e. q is computed from the detached epoch-boundary snapshot and frozen for the epoch, breaking target circularity.

loss_equations.name: assignment
loss_equations.equation: L_assign=-(1/(3*N)) sum_{i in I_train,l=1..3,k=1..256} Q[i,l,k]*log softmax_k(-D_c^2(P(z_i),P(e[l,k]))/0.05)
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: Q[N,3,256] is the detached soft transport target defined by the global assignment algorithm; logits[N,3,256] are differentiable.
loss_equations.index_normalization_reduction: Mean over N items and three levels; sum over 256 codes.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: Empty parent groups contribute no assignment; N=0 is invalid and NULL.
loss_equations.gradient_and_circularity: Gradient flows through differentiable logits to z,e. Q is from the detached epoch-boundary snapshot, including the explicitly initialized epoch-zero snapshot, and is frozen throughout the epoch; no same-step target dependence.

loss_equations.name: global_balance_anti_collapse
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: s[N,3,256] and m[3,256] are differentiable and computed in one deterministic full-training-population pass per epoch.
loss_equations.index_normalization_reduction: Mean marginal KL over three levels; sum over codes; coefficient 1.0 in L_total.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: No parent grouping is used; N=0 invalidates objective and yields NULL. All codes are included.
loss_equations.gradient_and_circularity: Gradient flows through m and s to z,e; fixed uniform reference is parameter-independent. This term is not calculated from q and therefore is not constant.

loss_equations.name: train_transition_prefix
loss_equations.tensors_and_shapes: T is the multiset of train-only observed directed item transitions, counted once per event; s[N,3,256] is differentiable. prefix2(t)=(q[t,1],q[t,2]); counts use frozen q and only successors of a sharing that prefix, with third code k.
loss_equations.index_normalization_reduction: Mean over T; sum over 256 codes. This is Stage2 item supervision, not ranking.
loss_equations.empty_group_rule: If T is empty L_tr=0 and omitted. A zero restricted successor count uses the smoothed p_pref distribution.
loss_equations.gradient_and_circularity: r and q are detached epoch-boundary targets, computed from training transitions only and frozen for the epoch. Gradient flows through s[t,3,:] to target z and level-three code vectors. No validation/test behavior enters.

math_definition.projection_order: For every vector: map (and apply any existing residual update), project to radius R, then assign/score. If subtractive residual operation is used: map residual input -> project residual input -> assign detached q -> subtract selected projected code -> project residual output -> score that projected residual. Projection is never deferred until after scoring. This candidate adds no residual architecture.
math_definition.loss_equations: See objective.loss_equations; each equation names tensors, shapes, indices, normalization, empty-group rule, gradient path and target-detachment rule.

hyperbolic_necessity: The selected failure is the strongly directed, sparse/tail next-item transition pattern evidenced by the train-only reverse-event fraction and directed-pair count. Negative curvature is a falsifiable hypothesis for representing uneven branching neighborhoods with less metric distortion than a flat metric; the supplied behavior aggregates do not prove hierarchy or recommendation gain.
euclidean_control: One implementation with identical architecture, parameter count, KMeans codebook initialization, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, budget, assignment procedure and fixed projection radius R=0.9 in both arms. The sole arm switch is the squared-distance operator: c=1 Poincare squared distance versus its exact c->0 replacement 4*||x-y||^2. No exponential map in either scoring path.
effect_site: Stage2 item-code geometry, global training-population assignment, reconstruction and commitment-style losses only. Stage2 emits one global three-token SID per item. No prefix Transformer, beam search, ranking metric or user bootstrap; frozen downstream T5 Stage3 ranks next items.
real_trigger_measurement: Use the frozen validation diagnostic definitions: over 52855 validation pairs (one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] to target), valid L1 positive hit rate is the share where anchor and positive first SID tokens match; valid Hard-L1 ER=10*positive_hits/negative_hits with negatives counted on the same ten negatives. level2_distinct_prefixes is the number of distinct (k1,k2) over all items. L3 collision is the share whose full SID is shared; L3 refinement gain is mean log2(level-2 bucket size/full-SID bucket size). Conditional G3 uses alpha=1,K=256: p_pref(l)=(items sharing target level-two prefix and third code l, minus one for target's own code, plus alpha)/(prefix bucket size minus one plus alpha*K); p_hist(l)=(train-only longest-prefix anchor successor count restricted to target prefix and third code l plus alpha*p_pref(l))/(restricted successor total plus alpha). G3 is mean log2(p_hist(target code)/p_pref(target code)); no restricted successor contributes zero, non-finite pair is NULL. Validation diagnostics never train Stage2.
training_only_inputs: Frozen content embeddings and train-split item transitions only. Whole-population assignment uses training item vectors/code vectors. Validation is diagnostic only; test/future events, prediction-time user context and batch composition are excluded from training and assignment targets.

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid_l1_hard_er
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Exact paired seeds [42,43,44]. For this metric independently compute each seed's curved-minus-flat value from the same validation pairs, then arithmetic mean the three differences. If any seed value is undefined/non-finite, the aggregate is NULL; otherwise compare aggregate strictly with this effect and apply the frozen admission gate valid_l1_hard_er strictly above 16.38953942232631 in each arm and seed.

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Exact paired seeds [42,43,44]. For this metric independently compute each seed's curved-minus-flat count over all items, then arithmetic mean the three differences. If any seed value is undefined/non-finite, the aggregate is NULL; otherwise compare strictly with this effect and apply the frozen admission gate level2_distinct_prefixes strictly above 16145 in each arm and seed.

stage2_diagnostics.name: l3_collision
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Exact paired seeds [42,43,44]; compute this metric's curved-minus-flat value per seed and arithmetic-mean all three. Any undefined/non-finite seed makes only this metric aggregate NULL; otherwise compare strictly with its registered direction/effect.

stage2_diagnostics.name: l3_refinement_gain
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Exact paired seeds [42,43,44]; compute this metric's curved-minus-flat value per seed and arithmetic-mean all three. Any undefined/non-finite seed makes only this metric aggregate NULL; otherwise compare strictly with its registered direction/effect.

stage2_diagnostics.name: conditional_g3
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: Exact paired seeds [42,43,44]; compute this metric's curved-minus-flat value per seed and arithmetic-mean all three. Any undefined/non-finite seed makes only this metric aggregate NULL; otherwise compare strictly with its registered direction/effect.

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: Exact paired seeds [42,43,44], using frozen T5 Stage3 on the held-out test split. For each seed compute curved-minus-flat test_R@10, then arithmetic mean the three paired differences. If either arm's result for any seed is undefined/non-finite, this metric aggregate alone is NULL; otherwise compare strictly with its registered effect.

classification.falsified_if: Any non-NULL registered diagnostic or behavioral aggregate fails its registered direction and minimum_effect comparison, or either frozen Stage2 admission gate is false in either arm for any seed.
classification.passed_if: Every registered diagnostic and behavioral aggregate is non-NULL and meets its registered direction and minimum_effect comparison, and both frozen Stage2 admission gates are true in both arms for every seed.
classification.mixed_if: Otherwise: in particular, any metric whose seed result or aggregate is undefined/non-finite (including zero denominator, missing evaluation or empty required stratum) is NULL and makes that metric comparison inconclusive. NULL propagation is metric-local: it neither passes nor falsifies that metric, and does not affect other metrics; any NULL comparison prevents overall passed classification.
